title: Where Does the Pattern Fit With At Most One Wrong Letter?

concept.title: A window matches with at most one mismatch exactly when its matching prefix and its matching suffix together cover all but one letter
body: Count the positions of a text where the pattern can be placed so that **at most one letter differs**. For the text `abcabd` and the pattern `abc`, the pattern fits at the position 1 exactly and at the position 4 with one wrong letter (`abd`), but not at the positions 2 and 3: the answer is 2. Comparing the pattern with every window letter by letter takes O(|t| |p|) steps.

For a window starting at `i`, let `pre` be the length of the longest common **prefix** of the pattern and the text from `i`, and `suf` the longest common **suffix** of the pattern and the text up to `i + m - 1` (with `m = |p|`). The window has at most one mismatch exactly when **`pre + suf >= m - 1`**: if the two matching parts overlap or touch, everything matches; if they leave a single letter between them, that one letter is the mismatch (it must differ, because `pre` is the longest). With two or more letters left over, there are at least two mismatches.

body.code:
zf = z_function(p + "#" + t)              # zf[m + 1 + i] = pre for the window at i
zr = z_function(p[::-1] + "#" + t[::-1])  # the same for the reversed words gives the suffixes
for i in range(n - m + 1):
    pre = zf[m + 1 + i]
    suf = zr[n + 1 - i]                   # the window ends at i + m - 1, i.e. at n - i - m in reverse
    if pre + suf >= m - 1: count += 1

body: The separator `#` keeps every Z value from running past the pattern. Two Z-function runs give all the `pre` and `suf` values in linear time, so the whole count is O(|t| + |p|).

statement: A text `t` and a pattern `p` are given. Count the positions `i` (from 1 to |t| - |p| + 1) such that the block of the text of length |p| that starts at `i` differs from `p` in **at most one** position. Print the count.
inputFormat: The first line has the text `t`.
The second line has the pattern `p`.
outputFormat: Print one number: the count of positions (0 if the pattern is longer than the text).
constraints: Both words have lowercase letters only.

examples.note: The windows abc (0 differences), bca (3), cab (3) and abd (1) give 2 good positions.

hints: For each window, let pre be the length of the matching prefix with the pattern, and suf the length of the matching suffix.
If pre + suf >= m - 1, the window has at most one mismatch.
Both values for all windows come from the Z-function: one run on pattern + # + text, and one on the reversed words.
